sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 is the south-eastern corner of the built-up part of the Borough of Merchantville, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned about 6 degrees. It is bounded by East Maple Avenue along the top, South Center Street on the left edge, Prospect Street on the right edge and, at the bottom, the borough line with Pensauken Township, below which Spruce Street runs along the foot of the sheet. Maple Terrace and Weikel Street run north and south through the middle, and Locust Street crosses the sheet about two thirds of the way down. The blocks are almost entirely frame dwellings with garages and outbuildings on long narrow lots, drawn in yellow, with several blue brick or concrete buildings: a row of stores and a block of flats on South Center Street at the upper left, a lodge hall lettered Knights of Columbus in the first block, and a church near the foot of Maple Terrace. In the lower left, between Maple Terrace and the South Center Street corner, three long blocks of attached dwellings face Merwit Court, and a lumber yard with its sheds fills the corner where Chapel Avenue and Magnolia Avenue run diagonally across the bottom left corner. Water pipes of 4, 6 and 8 inches are marked along the streets, and the street widths are lettered in feet. A compass rose and the oval Merchantville date stamp stand in the upper right block, and the scale bar is at the lower right.
notes: Weikel Street is Woodlawn Avenue today; South Center Street is South Centre Street; Magnolia Avenue is North Magnolia Avenue.
The borough boundary between Merchantville and Pensauken Township is lettered along the bottom of the sheet, just above Spruce Street.
50 ft. SE corner of the borough: E. Maple Av top, S. Center left, Prospect right, Spruce bottom (Weikel = Woodlawn Av); turned about 6 deg.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the west side of Merchantville between North and South Morris Avenue on the left and Alexander Avenue on the right, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned about 7 degrees. West Walnut Avenue runs along the top and West Maple Avenue along the bottom, and the sheet is divided across the middle by the Pennsylvania Railroad (Camden and Burlington County Railway branch), whose right of way is drawn four lines wide and marked 140 feet, not in scale. West Chestnut Avenue is lettered on both sides of the track, and the borough line between Merchantville and Pensauken Township runs along the north side of the railroad. The upper half is an area of new suburban building: Horner (Franklin) Avenue leads down from West Walnut Avenue into the West and East Hollywood Circle, a loop of 50 foot streets laid out around an inner block of lots, with detached frame dwellings, some of them not yet drawn on every lot. Large vacant tracts lie on the west side, and the borough line crosses diagonally through the upper right blocks. The lower half is a built-up residential block of frame dwellings fronting West Chestnut Avenue, with vacant ground in its middle. St. Peter's R.C. Church, its school and the rectory stand near the bottom, and a row of dwellings faces Alexander Avenue on the right. A compass rose and the oval Merchantville date stamp stand at the upper right, and the scale bar is at the bottom.
notes: Horner (Franklin) Avenue is Horner Avenue today; North and South Morris Avenue are Morris Street.
West Chestnut Avenue is drawn on both sides of the railroad; OpenStreetMap carries the north side as East Chestnut Avenue at Morris Street and the south side as West Chestnut Avenue.
The borough line between Merchantville and Pensauken Township runs along the north side of the railroad and then diagonally through the upper right blocks.
50 ft. West side, Morris to Alexander, W. Walnut to W. Maple; railroad across the middle; turned about 7.5 deg; fits 2.5 percent under sheets 2, 6, 7.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 is the commercial centre of the Borough of Merchantville, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned about 8 degrees. North and South Center Street run down the middle of the sheet, crossing West and East Walnut Avenue along the top, West and East Chestnut Avenue and the Pennsylvania Railroad (Camden and Burlington County Railway branch) across the upper middle, and West and East Maple Avenue at the bottom. West and East Park Avenue cut diagonally across the lower half from the lower left to the right edge, carrying 8 and 12 inch water mains. Alexander Avenue forms the left edge. The upper blocks are residential, with rows of frame dwellings along West Chestnut Avenue and West Walnut Avenue and a post office, a small store group and the American Legion hall beside North Center Street. South of the railroad lie the Merchantville Passenger Station and the lumber and coal yard of J. S. Collins and Son, with its long lumber sheds, coal pockets and Collins Hall. South Center Street and the Park Avenue diagonal carry the main business street: stores, the First National Bank, the fire department, a large Merchantville Garage, the Park Theatre, the Merchantville Inn near the lower left, the Municipal Building, a lodge rooms building and a flour and feed mill. Grace Church (Episcopal) and its Sunday school stand at the lower right. A compass rose and the oval Merchantville date stamp stand in the upper right block and the scale bar is at the lower right.
notes: North and South Center Street are North and South Centre Street today.

West Chestnut Avenue is drawn on both sides of the railroad; OpenStreetMap carries the north side of Chestnut Avenue east of Morris Street as East Chestnut Avenue, and the south side as West Chestnut Avenue.
The streets at the bottom edge of the sheet (East and West Maple Avenue) are cut by the sheet edge and are placed from their drawn north edge plus half the expected width.
The fitted scale is about 3 percent smaller than that of sheet 2.
50 ft. Town centre: Center St, Park Av diagonal, lumber yard; faint line work (ink 45 on the part); turned about 8.5 deg.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the east side of the Borough of Merchantville between the town centre and Cove Road, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned about 8 degrees. East Walnut Avenue runs along the top and East Maple Avenue along the bottom. Gilmore Avenue, Franklin Avenue, Clifton Avenue and Fithian Avenue run north and south, and East Chestnut Avenue is drawn on both sides of the Pennsylvania Railroad (Camden and Burlington County Railroad branch), which crosses the middle of the sheet with a curving siding and a wooden platform and freight house at the left. East Park Avenue comes in from the left edge and runs diagonally up to the right, with 8 and 12 inch water mains in it. The upper left blocks hold frame dwellings and outbuildings on deep lots. North of the railroad the diagonal blocks between East Park Avenue and Cove Road are laid out in narrow lots with dwellings, a filling station and a wagon and auto shop at their lower end. Cove Road runs along the upper right edge and is also the line between Merchantville and Pensauken Township. South of the railroad the blocks between East Park Avenue, East Chestnut Avenue and East Maple Avenue are mostly dwellings, with a church house, an auto repair shop and a few larger buildings. At the lower left stand the fire department (Niagara Fire Co.) and the Bell Telephone Exchange, and a part of the sheet is left blank where the neighbouring sheets carry the same ground. A compass rose and the oval Merchantville date stamp are in the upper right and the scale bar at the bottom.
notes: The streets at the bottom edge (East Maple Avenue) and the right edge (Fithian Avenue) are cut by the sheet edge, so their junctions rest on one drawn edge plus the expected half width.
East Chestnut Avenue is drawn on both sides of the railroad; the modern nodes for it do not agree with the drawn rows to better than about 4 m.
50 ft. East side: Gilmore, Franklin, Clifton, Fithian, E. Park, Cove Rd; railroad across the middle; weakly controlled (4 points, 2 hand-picked).

sheet-6.description: Sheet 6 shows the north-west part of the Borough of Merchantville, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned about 8 degrees, between West Rogers Avenue at the top and West Walnut Avenue at the bottom. Horner (Franklin) Avenue runs north and south through the middle of the sheet and Leslie Avenue along the right edge, and West Cedar Avenue crosses both. A lane lettered Whitman Terrace (Merchantville Avenue) runs east and west just above West Walnut Avenue, and Merchantville Avenue itself cuts diagonally across the lower left corner, with North Morris Avenue and the lower end of Horner Avenue running off the bottom edge. The district is residential: detached frame dwellings with small garages and outbuildings stand on narrow lots along each street, a few built of concrete block (marked C.B.) or tile, and several larger tile-and-stucco houses stand near Leslie Avenue. The blocks at the upper left are large and thinly built, and a block between West Cedar Avenue and Whitman Terrace is largely vacant. The borough line between Merchantville and Pensauken Township crosses the lower right blocks as a dash and dot line, running from the lower right up to the right edge. House numbers are printed twice along most streets, the old numbers above the new. A slanting left margin shows where the sheet is cut off, and a compass rose stands at the left; the oval Merchantville date stamp is at the top right and the scale bar at the bottom.
notes: The north-south street lettered Horner (Franklin) Avenue is Horner Avenue today; North Morris Avenue is Morris Street.
West Rogers Avenue was left out of the fit: its modern line lies about 9 m from the drawn street.

The diagonal Horner Avenue below West Walnut Avenue is the street that meets West Walnut Avenue at the modern node Horner Avenue / Walnut Avenue; the north-south Horner (Franklin) Avenue has no node of its own at West Walnut Avenue.
50 ft. NW area: Horner (Franklin) Av, Whitman Ter, W. Cedar, W. Rogers (W. Rogers and Merchantville Av left out as displaced).

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 shows the north-central part of the Borough of Merchantville, drawn at 50 ft to an inch and turned about 8 degrees, between West Rogers Avenue at the top and West Walnut Avenue at the bottom. Leslie Avenue forms the left edge and North Center Street the right edge, and Penn runs north from West Cedar Avenue in the upper left. West Cedar Avenue crosses the sheet about halfway down, and the short ends of East Rogers Avenue, East Cedar Avenue and East Walnut Avenue are lettered at the right edge. The sheet is almost wholly residential: rows of detached frame dwellings with garages and outbuildings stand on long narrow lots, a few built of concrete block (marked C.B.) or tile, and a small number of stores are drawn near North Center Street at the lower right. The Womens Club of Merchantville stands in the upper right blocks. A dash and dot line crossing the sheet from the lower left to the upper right is the borough line, lettered Pensauken Twp. on one side and Merchantville on the other, and it cuts diagonally through the blocks above West Cedar Avenue. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are marked in the streets, and street widths are lettered as 50 feet. The compass rose and the oval Merchantville date stamp are at the top and the scale bar is at the bottom.
notes: North Center Street is North Centre Street today; Penn is Penn Street.
West Rogers Avenue was not used: it was left out of the fit on sheet 6, where its modern line lies about 9 m from the drawn street.
The fit is unusually tight: five junctions, four of them water-pipe crossings, agree to 0.25 m.
50 ft. North-central: Penn, Leslie, N. Center, W. Cedar; borough line diagonal.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and covers a district of Pensauken Township on the north-eastern side of the Merchantville borough line. North Center Street runs down the left edge, crossed from top to bottom by East Rogers Avenue, East Cedar Avenue and East Walnut Avenue, which lead east to Gilmore Avenue and to Cove Road, a wide street that crosses the upper right of the sheet on the diagonal with the Pensauken Twp and Merchantville boundary line drawn along its middle. A second stretch of the boundary line crosses the upper left corner above East Rogers Avenue. East Walnut Avenue turns north-east beyond Gilmore Avenue to follow Cove Road, and Githens Avenue is shown as a short street meeting Cove Road from the east. The blocks are lined with detached frame dwellings with outbuildings, a few of stone, and scattered coops and sheds; the lots are long and narrow, and the blocks between Gilmore Avenue and Cove Road and the lower part of the sheet are largely empty. The only large building is the 1st Baptist Church at the corner of North Center Street and East Walnut Avenue. Water pipes of 4 and 6 inches are marked in the streets. The sheet is a plain street map without insets; the adjoining sheets are keyed 4, 5, 7, 15, 20 and 21, and the block numbers 51, 52, 55, 56 and 59 appear on it.
notes: North Center is North Centre Street in OpenStreetMap; East Rogers Avenue is Rogers Avenue; Cove Road keeps its name.
The Gilmore Avenue / East Walnut Avenue junction was left out of the fit: the drawn street bends there and the modern node lies about 9 m from the drawn crossing.
50 ft. N. Center / E. Rogers, E. Cedar, E. Walnut, Gilmore, Cove Rd; borough line crosses.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and covers the border between the City of Camden, Pensauken Township and the Borough of Merchantville west of Merchantville proper, a district laid out on a diagonal grid. West Chestnut Avenue runs along the top of the sheet. Below it 41st, 42nd and 43rd Streets run down the page from north-west to south-east, crossed by Crescent Boulevard, which runs diagonally from the lower left to the upper right. The blocks along 41st Street and 43rd Street are lined with detached frame dwellings, with a few outbuildings, and one brick building near Crescent Boulevard; the blocks between 42nd Street and West End Avenue are largely vacant. A cement-block garage for 15 cars and a gasoline station stand near the centre. In the lower left, on the Camden side of the City of Camden and Pensauken Twp line, Roosevelt Avenue and the long 42nd Street frontage carry rows of brick stores and apartments, an auto sales building and long party-wall rows of dwellings with garages behind, along Carman and the angled Harding Road (Carman). Federal and West Maple Avenue, marked as this side of the street, cross the lower part of the sheet; West End Avenue runs down the right side beside a dash-dot line marking the boundary between the Borough of Merchantville and Pensauken Township, with dwellings along its west side, and Myrtle Avenue crosses at the bottom. The left margin is lettered See Map of Camden N.J. Volume Two. The compass stands at the lower right. Adjoining sheets are keyed 10, 11, 25 and the Camden volume.
notes: In OpenStreetMap West End Avenue meets North 42nd Street and Maple Avenue at one node, so the drawn 42nd Street and West End Avenue read as one street changing its name.
Harding Road (Carman) is Harding Road today; the modern Carmen Street / Harding Road node lies about 12 m from the drawn crossing, so it was left out of the fit.

Placed from three points only (41st Street / Crescent Boulevard detected, West End Avenue / West Maple Avenue and West End Avenue / Myrtle Avenue hand-picked from the pipes and lot lines): low confidence.
The map note See Map of Camden N.J. Volume Two refers to the neighbouring Camden volume.
50 ft. Diagonal Pennsauken grid at the Camden line: 41st-43rd Sts, Crescent Blvd, West End Av, W. Maple; 3 control points only (low confidence).

sheet-10.description: Sheet 10 is drawn at 50 ft to an inch and covers the south-western corner of the Borough of Merchantville and the adjoining part of Pensauken Township. The railroad of the Camden and Burlington County Railway branch crosses the top of the sheet along West Chestnut Avenue. Below it the blocks between South Poplar Avenue, Euclid Avenue and Clinton Avenue are lined with detached frame and brick dwellings on narrow lots, with a few garages and outbuildings. A diagonal line marks the boundary between the Borough of Merchantville and Pensauken Township and separates the 43rd Street frontage at the left, where several dwellings and then two brick apartment buildings and a row of apartments with courts face the street, from the borough. Along West Maple Avenue, labelled on its Pensauken side as Federal, stand the commercial buildings: a long brick showroom block with garages behind, a large garage and repair shop for 60 cars and another for 40 cars, and a row of brick stores with party walls. East of South Poplar Avenue, Wellwood Manor Apartment and Wedgewood Walk form two U-shaped brick apartment courts facing a central walk. West End Avenue, a diagonal street, runs down the left edge and meets Myrtle Avenue at the bottom, where South Hamilton Avenue runs down the right side beside the blank block numbered 10 and the next sheet, 27. Six-inch and four-inch water pipes are marked in the streets. The compass at the lower left points up and to the right. Neighbouring sheets are keyed 9, 11, 12, 25, 26 and 27.
notes: South Poplar is Poplar Avenue today; South Hamilton Avenue is Hamilton Avenue and Clinton Avenue is offset from it across West Maple Avenue.
Hamilton Avenue / West Maple Avenue and Hamilton Avenue / Myrtle Avenue are hand-picked on the centre of the drawn street edges (the detector found no junction on the sparsely drawn street).
The lettering of v in Merchantville looks like u on some of the boundary labels.
50 ft. Crescent Blvd, 43rd St, W. Chestnut, Poplar, Curtis, Euclid, Clinton, Federal, W. Maple, West End, S. Hamilton, Myrtle.

sheet-11-1.description: The main part of sheet 11 covers a regular grid of building lots in Pennsauken Township north-west of Merchantville, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned about 34 degrees so that the numbered streets run up the page. It runs from Remington Avenue near the top down to Westfield Avenue at the bottom, and from 41st Street on the left to 47th Street or Chapman Avenue on the right, with Amon Avenue and High Street crossing the middle. The upper half, lettered Delaware Gardens, is cut into narrow lots of which only a few carry frame dwellings and garages. The lower half, lettered Amon Heights Tract No. 2, is more built up: between 44th and 45th Streets below Amon Avenue stand long rows of attached brick and frame houses, and further rows run along High Street. A moving picture theatre of brick fills the corner of Westfield Avenue and 47th Street, and a stone contractor's yard lies near 47th Street. A heavy line along the left side and the lower left corner marks the edge of the area covered by the Camden atlas (lettered See Map of Camden Volume Two); the area beyond Westfield Avenue is left blank with the same note. The lower left corner of the page holds a separate inset drawn at another angle (part 2).
notes: 47th Street is lettered '47th St. or Chapman Av.'.
The area names are lettered spread across the blocks; Delaware Gardens covers the upper half, Amon Heights Tract No. 2 the lower half.
Beyond the heavy line on the left and below Westfield Avenue the sheet refers to the Camden atlas, volume two.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main map (Delaware Gardens / Amon Heights Tract No. 2, 41st to 47th Streets, Remington Av to Westfield Av, turned about 34 deg); 2 inset in the lower left behind a heavy line, turned so north points left (46th/45th Streets at Crescent Blvd and W. Chestnut Av, Pennsauken edge of Camden). Area beyond the heavy line and below Westfield Av refers to the Camden atlas vol. 2.

sheet-11-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 11 is an inset in the lower left corner of the page, cut off from the main map by a heavy line and drawn at 100 ft to an inch but turned so that north points to the left (its own north arrow). It shows a small area of Pennsauken Township on the edge of Camden around Crescent Boulevard, between 47th Street at the top and 45th Street near the bottom, and from Jackson Avenue on the left edge to West Chestnut Avenue on the right, where West Chestnut Avenue is drawn on both sides of the Pennsylvania Railroad's Camden and Burlington County Railway Division. 46th Street becomes North Euclid east of Crescent Boulevard, and North Poplar leaves the boulevard towards West Chestnut Avenue; Williams Avenue is a short street south of Crescent Boulevard. The blocks hold scattered frame dwellings and garages, with a foundation drawn on 46th Street and a scenic paint works at the bottom edge; many lots are vacant.
notes: Inset turned on the page: north points to the left.
North Euclid is the stretch of today's 46th Street east of Crescent Boulevard; North Poplar is today's 45th Street east of the boulevard.
The west side of West Chestnut Avenue is North Chestnut Avenue in OpenStreetMap; the two carriageways lie either side of the railroad.
Crescent Boulevard is today's North Crescent Boulevard (US 130); its junctions fit 2 to 3 m off, and the inset as a whole fits at about 4 percent under the atlas scale (RMSE 3.9 m): low confidence.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 is drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points up and to the right. Its upper third shows the part of Pensauken Township north of the Merchantville borough line, where Crescent Boulevard crosses the page diagonally and 47th, 48th and 49th Streets run down from it toward the railroad, with North Browning Road (also lettered North Wellwood Avenue) at the right. Below the railroad is the built-up south-western corner of Merchantville: Clinton, Linden and Irvin Avenues, South Browning Road, North and South Lexington Avenues, North and South Springfield Avenues and North and South Morris Avenues run north and south between West Chestnut Avenue and West Maple Avenue. The blocks hold frame dwellings with garages and outbuildings, mostly on lots 40 to 50 ft wide, with a few brick and tile houses. South Browning Road crosses the lower left corner diagonally, marked with 8 and 12 inch water mains, and the rest of the lower sheet is blank. The compass stands at the top left. Adjoining sheets are keyed 3, 6, 10, 11, 13, 14 and 27.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers the north-western part of Pennsauken Township next to the Borough of Merchantville, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 33 degrees so that north points up and to the right. Westfield Avenue runs along the top, Crescent Boulevard along the bottom, and Mechantville Avenue (the spelling printed on the sheet) forms the right edge, with sheet 17 above, sheet 14 to the right and sheet 12 below. Church and a Lutheran temple stand on the blocks beside Westfield Avenue, and a row of brick and masonry buildings faces Westfield Avenue near 49th Street. South of Camden Avenue the narrow 47th, 48th and 49th Streets run down the left side to Crescent Boulevard, lined with dwellings on deep lots, and block 43, a large open tract with the compass rose, fills the middle. sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 shows the Hillcrest district on the Pennsauken Township side of the Merchantville line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 41 degrees clockwise. Westfield Avenue forms the top edge and Crescent Boulevard cuts diagonally across the lower left, with Merchantville Avenue along the left side and Scovel Avenue on the right. Camden Avenue (Road) runs across the upper third beside the Public Service Railway Company right of way, and Hillcrest Avenue (Road) and Horner Avenue run down through the middle. The blocks between Westfield Avenue and Wayne Avenue (Cramer) are mostly built with frame dwellings, with some brick houses. Two long rows of attached houses stand on the narrow lots beside Merchantville and Hollinshed Avenues on the left, with a smaller group of brick dwellings at the top of Hillcrest Avenue near a laundry (Hillcrest Laundry) and a church (Hillcrest Community Church). The Pensauken Graded and Junior High School, a large brown building with a gymnasium and auditorium, stands in block 76 at the lower left. South of Upsal the ground is largely vacant, and below Crescent Boulevard the diagonal streets W. Harvey, W. Irving and W. Rogers Avenues and Horner (Franklin) Avenue are only partly built. sheet-15.description: Sheet 15 covers the southern edge of the Hillcrest district and the north-eastern corner of the Borough of Merchantville, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 17 degrees. A boundary line between Pensauken Township and Merchantville crosses the lower right corner near East Rogers Avenue. South of West Harvey Avenue the blocks between Horner (Franklin) Avenue, Penn and North Center are lined with frame houses on deep lots down to West and East Rogers Avenue, and a brick building with stores stands on North Center near East Irving Avenue. sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 shows Delaware Gardens, a subdivision of Pennsauken Township on the Delaware River, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 58 degrees so that north points to the upper left. The Delaware River and the Pennsylvania Railroad (Trenton Division) run down the left edge, with Riverside Drive beside the tracks. River Road runs from top to bottom through the middle of the sheet, crossed by Merchantville Avenue, Springfield Avenue (East River Drive), North Lexington Avenue (53rd Street), Tinsman Avenue (52nd Street), 49th (50th) Street, 48th (49th) Street, West River Drive and 47th Street or Chapman Avenue. Forrest Avenue and Glendale Avenue run in the right half, and North Browning Road crosses it from the middle to the right edge. The Merchantville Water Company pumping station stands where Forrest Avenue meets North Browning Road, with the Delaware Gardens Volunteer Fire Company beside it, and the Delaware Gardens Community Baptist Church stands on West River Drive. The word No Exposure is printed along the top. Sheet 17 lies to the right, sheet 18 above and sheet 11 below.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 shows the eastern part of Delaware Gardens, a platted subdivision of Pennsauken Township, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 58 degrees so that north points to the upper left. Merchantville Avenue runs across the top and Westfield Avenue forms the right edge, with sheet 18 above, sheet 13 to the right and sheet 11 below. The horizontal streets are Springfield Avenue (East River Drive), North Lexington Avenue (53rd Street), Tinsman Avenue (52nd Street), North Browning Road, 49th (50th) Street, 48th (49th) Street, West River Drive and 47th Street or Chapman Avenue at the bottom. The curving streets Pleasant and High, with Forrest Avenue and Glendale Avenue at the left edge, cross them. The lots are very narrow and deep, laid out in numbered blocks 1 to 32, and the houses are almost all frame dwellings of one and a half or two storeys with small outbuildings, thickest between Pleasant and High and along Westfield Avenue. Near the Westfield Avenue edge a block of brick and masonry buildings stands in block 4, and at the lower right a pair of brick dwellings and others are drawn in block 1. The lettering Delaware Gardens is spread across the blocks. The Merchantville date stamp and the compass rose are at the top. sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers the north-eastern end of the Pennsauken Township district around Hollinshed and Hillcrest Avenues, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 57 degrees so that north points to the upper left. The top of the sheet is blank paper marked No Exposure, with Arlington Cemetery lettered along its edge, and Cove Road runs diagonally across the upper part from lower left to upper right. Westfield Avenue forms the right edge. Pleasant, Amon Road (Thomas Avenue), High and Lincoln (Manor) Avenue run down through the sheet and are crossed by Scovel Avenue, Horner Avenue (59th Street), Hillcrest Avenue (58th Street), Hollinshed Avenue (57th Street), Gross Avenue (56th Street) and Merchantville Avenue at the bottom. The streets are laid out in blocks of very narrow lots, mostly vacant, with frame dwellings clustered in blocks 7, 8, 9, 3, 13 and 14. The Longfellow Public School, a fire-proof steel and concrete building put up in 1926, stands at the lower left. Large spaced lettering along High reads State Highway. At the upper right the end of the street grid carries Marlon Avenue, Penn Street and Mulford and Scovel Avenues. Sheet 17 lies below, sheet 14 to the right and sheet 19 beyond the top right corner.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 covers the northern part of Merchantville Borough and the adjoining Pensauken Township land around Crescent Boulevard, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned about 39 degrees, so that the streets run steeply across the page and north points to the upper right. Westfield Avenue crosses the top of the sheet below Arlington Cemetery, and Grant (Highland) Avenue closes it at the bottom. sheet-20.description: Sheet 20 shows the north-western part of Pensauken Township at the edge of Merchantville, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned about 39 degrees, with north toward the upper right. A regular grid of blocks (numbers 126 to 138 and 434 to 437, 708 to 710) lies between Grant (Highland) Avenue at the top and East Cedar Avenue at the bottom, and between Cove Road at the left edge and the Pennsylvania Railroad branch on the right, where a diagonal band of tracks carries the legend of the Delaware River Railroad and Bridge Co branch. Cove Road crosses the lower part of the sheet from lower left to right, marking the boundary between Pensauken Township and the Borough of Merchantville. In the upper left the Cooper (Cattell) and Cooper (Washington) Avenues run along the top with large blocks 144 to 150, with a coal and tank yard and the Atlantic City railroad running diagonally across the sheet on a bridge. sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 shows the Pensauken Township district around Union and Marion Avenues, north of Sheet 21, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned about 60 degrees. South Gladwyn (Pensauken) Avenue runs across the upper part below Howard Avenue and Acme Place, and Cooper (Cattell) and Cooper (Washington) Avenues close the sheet at the bottom. E. The best-built area is on the right between Pennsylvania, North Finlaw and Elm Avenues, where Marion Avenue (Centre) and Church Avenue are lined with frame dwellings, and the Pensauken M. E. Church (built 1886-1893) stands on Pennsylvania Avenue. Pensauken Township Public School No. 5 stands off South Union Avenue, and the Pensauken Athletic Club and baseball grounds are at the bottom. At upper left Acme Place, Howard Avenue and Marion Avenue run down the left edge, and Argus Street is at the upper right. The compass rose is at upper left.

The left side of the sheet follows the boundary between the City of Camden and Pensauken Township, a heavy dash-dot line running from the lower left up to the right and lettered See Camden Volume Two along the margin. sheet-27.description: Sheet 27 covers the south-western edge of the Borough of Merchantville and the adjoining part of Pennsauken Township, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned about 8 degrees so that north points slightly right of up. The sheet runs from Clinton Street and West Maple Avenue at the top down to Magnolia Avenue at the bottom, and from South Hamilton Avenue on the left edge to South Morris Avenue on the right. sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 covers the built-up centre of Merchantville and the adjoining part of Pennsauken Township, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned about 11 degrees clockwise so that north points up and slightly right. West Maple Avenue and East Maple Avenue run across the top, with South Morris Avenue down the left edge and South Center Street down the right. The diagonal line of Chapel Avenue crosses the sheet from the top near West Maple Avenue to the lower right, past the Merchantville High School, which has an auditorium and a fire-proof main building on the block between Chapel Avenue and South Center Street, and the First Presbyterian Church at East Maple Avenue. Trinity M. E. Church stands on West Maple Avenue. North of the Merchantville and Pennsauken Township boundary, which crosses the middle of the sheet, the blocks along Volan and Stanley are mostly frame dwellings, with several large vacant tracts. South of it, in Pennsauken Township, a close grid of long narrow blocks runs between Victoria, Russel (New), Clayton, Magnolia, Wisteria and Merchant on one axis and Penn, Scovel, Horner and Millers on the other, filled with small frame dwellings and a few brick and tile buildings, among them the Pennsauken Township public school (colored), Asbury M. E. Church and a Baptist church (colored) beside Spruce Street at the right edge. A second boundary line between Pennsauken and Delaware townships runs along the lower part of the sheet. At the lower left, Jefferson Avenue, Willow Street and Cherry Street run through largely vacant blocks. A compass rose and the Merchantville stamp stand on the right margin, and the scale bar at the bottom left.
notes: Penn Avenue (Front) is Penn Street today; Magnolia Avenue is North Magnolia Avenue; Horner (3rd Street) is Horner Street; Millers Avenue is Miller Avenue; Merchant is Merchant Street; Russel (New) is Russell Avenue; Victoria is Victoria Street; South Center is South Centre Street; South Morris Avenue is Morris Street.
Miller Avenue lies about 5 m from its drawn line; it was left out of the control points.
100 ft. Turned +11 deg. South Merchantville and Pennsauken Twp, Chapel Av diagonal (ink 30 on the part); Miller Av left out as displaced.

sheet-29-1.description: The main part of sheet 29 covers the south-eastern corner of the Borough of Merchantville and the edge of Delaware Township, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with north about 6 degrees right of up. It runs from Rudderow Avenue at the top to Sussex Avenue near the bottom, and from Prospect Street on the left edge to the railroad on the right. East Maple Avenue crosses the upper third; Cove Road and Church Road cut diagonally across the sheet, Church Road forming part of the line between Pensauken Township and Merchantville. The north-south streets are Fithian Avenue, Greenleigh Court (drawn 80 ft wide with a park strip down its middle), Westminster Avenue, St. James Avenue, Plymouth Place and Bethel (Allan) Avenue. North of East Maple Avenue the blocks along Rudderow Avenue carry rows of frame dwellings, a concrete-block garage for twenty cars and some stores; south of it the blocks to Somerset and Sussex Avenues are residential, with an apartment house at East Maple Avenue and Prospect Street. The left side of the lower half is the Merchantville Country Club with tennis courts and golf links. The Delaware River Railroad and Bridge Company (Pennsylvania Railroad) runs down the right side past the Maple Inn, beyond which the sheet is left blank (sheet 32). The borough line between Merchantville and Delaware Township crosses the lower part of the sheet. The lower left corner of the page holds a separate inset (part 2).
notes: St. James Avenue is Saint James Place today.

Somerset Avenue was left out of the control: both its junctions fitted 5 to 6 m off in the same direction, with Sussex and East Maple Avenues agreeing; the sheet's north-south spacing is about 6 percent shorter than its east-west spacing against the modern streets.
Prospect Street, drawn along the left edge, was left out: the detector took a lot line for it.
Maple Inn stands beside the railroad at the upper right.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main map (E. Maple Av, Rudderow to Sussex Avs, Fithian to Bethel Avs, railroad on the right, Merchantville Country Club); 2 inset lower left behind a heavy line: south side of Spruce St at Orchard and Prospect (Merchantville), anchored on one hand-picked point.

sheet-29-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 29 is a small inset in the lower left corner of the page, set off by a heavy line and drawn at 100 ft to an inch with north nearly straight up (its own north arrow). It shows the south side of Spruce, also lettered Weikel Street, in Merchantville from the left edge to Prospect, with Orchard crossing it and running south through the golf course of the country club. The row of lots on the south side of Spruce, numbered 24 to 48, carries frame dwellings of two and two and a half stories and a few garages, with two more houses and a tool store on the golf course behind them. The line between Merchantville and Delaware Township (lettered Pensauken Township on one side) crosses the inset along Spruce. The north side of the street is drawn on sheet 2, and the area to the left continues on sheet 28.
notes: Spruce is Spruce Street today. Orchard (Orchard St. on sheet 2) south of Spruce is a service road in OpenStreetMap (Orchard Avenue) whose junction does not match the drawn street well.
Placed from two points carried from sheet 2 (Prospect and Orchard at Spruce, street centres drawn on both sheets), with the atlas scale (3.92 px/ft) and north 6 degrees right of up: low confidence.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main map (E. Maple Av, Rudderow to Sussex Avs, Fithian to Bethel Avs, railroad on the right, Merchantville Country Club); 2 inset lower left behind a heavy line: south side of Spruce St at Orchard and Prospect (Merchantville), anchored on one hand-picked point.

sheet-30.description: Sheet 30 covers the Pennsauken Township and Delaware Township side of the Merchantville area east of the borough, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned about 4 degrees so that north points slightly right of up. The Pennsylvania Railroad Camden and Burlington County branch crosses the top edge, with the railroad station at the upper left. Collins Lane, partly marked not opened, runs along the top of the first row of blocks, and Rudderow Avenue and East Maple Avenue cross the sheet from left to right. Between them the blocks of South Finlaw, Union, Willis, Volney, Manor and Gladwyn Avenues carry frame dwellings, and a row of six similar pink-coloured brick dwellings stands on Manor Avenue at the right. The boundary between Pensauken Township and Delaware Township runs diagonally from the lower left to the right edge just below East Maple Avenue. South of it a garage building stands beside South Finlaw Avenue, and the long narrow blocks of Willis, Wilbur and Volney Avenues are lined with small frame dwellings. Haddonfield Road runs diagonally down the right side with Pennsylvania Avenue beside it, and Carlisle, Trinity, Vassar and Yale Avenues cross it in largely vacant blocks. Harvard Avenue crosses the lower third of the sheet; below it Wilbur Avenue, Willis Street, Princeton Avenue and Dickinson Avenue are laid out on mostly empty blocks, with Elm Avenue and Church Road at the lower left. Overbrook Drive and Wayne Road run in the right margin, and a compass rose and scale bar stand at the bottom right.
notes: East Maple Avenue is Maple Avenue today; South Finlaw Avenue is Finlaw Avenue.
Collins Lane is marked not opened along part of its length; its junctions with Volney and Union Avenues lie about 10 m from the drawn lines and were not used.
The Pennsylvania Railroad Camden and Burlington County branch is lettered along the top edge.
100 ft. Turned +5 deg. E. Maple / Rudderow east of the borough, Haddonfield Rd (ink 30 on the part).

sheet-31-1.description: The main part of sheet 31 covers a newly laid-out suburban tract in Delaware Township, east of Merchantville, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with north about 7 degrees right of up. It runs from East Maple Avenue along the top, where the boundary line between Pensauken Township and Delaware Township follows the street, down past Media Road to Overbrook Drive, and from Haddonfield Road on the left to Merion Road on the right. The north-south streets are Bala, Ambler, St. Davids, St. Martins, Lenape and Merion Roads, crossed by Wayne Road in the upper left and Media Road through the middle; Overbrook Drive curves across the lower half and turns south past Lenape Road towards Manheim Drive at the bottom. Carlisle Avenue, St. Martins Avenue and New York Avenue (marked not opened) leave East Maple Avenue northwards at the top edge. The blocks are divided into large numbered lots with only scattered frame and brick-veneer dwellings and garages, and a pair of stores at East Maple Avenue and Bala Road; most of the land is vacant. The lower left corner of the page holds a separate inset of another area (part 2), cut off by a heavy line.
notes: East Maple Avenue here is Maple Avenue today.
The boundary line between Pensauken and Delaware Townships is drawn along East Maple Avenue.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main map (Delaware Twp tract: E. Maple Av = Maple Av, Wayne, Bala, Ambler, St Davids, St Martins, Lenape, Merion Rds, Media Rd, Overbrook Dr); 2 inset lower left behind a heavy line (Collins Lane, Rudderow Av, E. Maple Av between Taylor Av = Cooper Av and S. Finlaw Av, Pennsauken Twp).

sheet-31-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 31 is an inset filling the lower left of the page below a heavy line, drawn at 100 ft to an inch at nearly the same angle as the main map but showing a separate area of Pensauken Township west of the main part. Along its top runs the Pennsylvania Railroad's Camden and Burlington County Branch, with Collins Lane (partly not opened) just south of it. Below are the blocks between Collins Lane, Rudderow Avenue and East Maple Avenue, from Taylor Avenue on the left to South Finlaw Avenue on the right, with Burling Avenue between them and a short not-named, not-opened street. Frame dwellings stand in rows along Collins Lane, Rudderow Avenue and South Finlaw Avenue; at East Maple Avenue and Burling Avenue are an auto repair shop, a store and a filling station, and a concrete-block bowling alley stands near the left edge. The large lots west of Taylor Avenue are vacant.
notes: Taylor Avenue is Cooper Avenue today; East Maple Avenue is Maple Avenue.
Burling Avenue / Collins Lane was left out: the modern junction fits about 6 m off the drawn one, where Collins Lane was not yet opened.

Maple Av = Maple Av, Wayne, Bala, Ambler, St Davids, St Martins, Lenape, Merion Rds, Media Rd, Overbrook Dr); 2 inset lower left behind a heavy line (Collins Lane, Rudderow Av, E. Maple Av between Taylor Av = Cooper Av and S. Finlaw Av, Pennsauken Twp).

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 covers the southern edge of the Merchantville area, partly in the Borough of Merchantville and partly in Delaware Township, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned about 24 degrees so that north points up and to the left. Church Road runs across the top, with the numbered avenues 1st to 5th and South Finlaw Avenue ending against it in blocks marked as belonging to other sheets, and a double railroad (the Delaware River R.R. and Bridge Co. line) runs down the left edge with an iron bridge at the top corner. A diagonal dash-dot line is the boundary between the Borough of Merchantville and Delaware Township. Close to the boundary the lots are narrow, and the blocks between Glenwood Avenue, Holly Avenue, Ivins Avenue and State, and between Barlow, Linderman and Petitt Avenues south to Holly Street and Thomas, are filled with regular rows of small frame dwellings with their street numbers. Some streets near the top, such as one west of Ivins Avenue, are marked not opened. Glenwood, Monroe and Grant Avenues cut diagonally across the lower left, and below them Monroe, Lincoln and Union Avenues run south through very long, thinly built lots with scattered dwellings and a few small works. State runs along the right edge, with Dudley Avenue at the right margin. A compass rose and scale bar stand at the left.
notes: Grant Avenue is West Grant Avenue; Lincoln Avenue is Lincoln Avenue North; State is State Street.
The spaced letters MERCHANTVILLE MANOR (left half) and MERCHANTVILLE TERRACE (right half) are lettered across the blocks, as on the key map.
The Delaware River R.R. and Bridge Co. railroad and an iron bridge are drawn at the left edge.
100 ft. Turned -24 deg. Church Rd to Monroe/Lincoln/Union; Merchantville Manor and Terrace; Delaware River RR on the left edge (ink 30 on the part).

sheet-33.description: Sheet 33 covers the south-western edge of the Merchantville district, in Delaware Township, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned about 8 degrees so that north points up and slightly to the left. A railroad corridor (the Pennsylvania Railroad's Delaware River R.R. and Bridge Co. branch) runs from top to bottom through the left third of the sheet, crossed by Chapel Avenue on an iron bridge. Chapel Avenue is the main diagonal, running from the upper left past Evergreen Avenue and across the sheet to Highland Avenue at the lower right, and State is a second wide diagonal running north-east from its crossing with Monroe Avenue. North of State the long blocks of Monroe, Lincoln and Union Avenues are almost empty, with a few dwellings and a store. Between State and Chapel Avenue, along Princeton and Yale Avenues, narrow lots run back from the streets with scattered frame dwellings and some larger buildings in blue and pink fill. West of the railroad Kenilworth Avenue runs down the left side, with Helena, Edward, Jerome and Longwood Avenues branching from it into blocks with a few dwellings. South of Chapel Avenue stand Joseph Hinchman Public School, the Woodland M. E. Chapel and the Woodland Fire Co. building, among Northwood, Beechwood, Hollywood, Poplar and Highland Avenues. Harvard Avenue is at the right edge, a compass rose is in the upper left centre and the scale bar at the bottom.
notes: Chapel Avenue is Chapel Avenue West today; State is State Street; Lincoln Avenue is Lincoln Avenue North.
Several Chapel Avenue West junctions (Evergreen, Princeton, Harvard) lie 4 to 6 m from the drawn junctions, and the fit has a leave-one-out error of about 5 m.
An iron bridge carries Chapel Avenue over the railroad.
100 ft. Turned -8 deg. Chapel Av West / State / Princeton area; Chapel junctions scatter 4-6 m (ink 30 on the part); weak.

sheet-34.description: Sheet 34 covers an area of Delaware Township south-east of Merchantville, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned only about 2 degrees. Dudley Avenue runs across the top, with Petitt Avenue, Victor and Woodland Avenue (north of Dudley) meeting it from above, and the Haddonfield Avenue line runs down the right-hand edge of the sheet. State runs down the left side and then turns south-west toward the edge. A diagonal line crosses the block between State and Woodland Avenue, which here runs from the top of the sheet to the bottom. Most of the sheet is long narrow lots at roughly 50 ft frontage, mostly vacant, with scattered frame dwellings and sheds in the blocks between Woodland Avenue, 3rd Avenue and Haddonfield Avenue. The more built-up part is at the left, along Princeton Avenue and Yale Avenue, where dwellings and stores line the blocks and the Merchantville Hosiery Co. Inc. works, a pink and yellow building with steam heat, electric lights and bucket extinguishers, stands beside Woodland Avenue. Princeton Avenue also crosses the right-hand blocks, and Harvard Avenue closes the sheet at the bottom. Large parts of the sheet carry no exposure along the top and right margins. A compass rose stands at the left and the scale bar at the bottom.
notes: State is State Street today; Victor is Victor Avenue; Haddonfield Avenue is Haddonfield Road.
The Dudley Avenue, Petitt Avenue and State junction measured 5 m off the others and was left out of the control points.
100 ft. Nearly north up. Woodland, Dudley, Princeton, Yale; vacant long lots (ink 30 on the part).

sheet-35-1.description: The main part of sheet 35 covers thinly built-up land in Delaware Township south-east of Merchantville, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with north about 7 degrees left of up. Chapel Avenue crosses the sheet diagonally from the upper left to the lower right, meeting Haddonfield Avenue (today's Haddonfield Road), which runs down the right side. Harvard Avenue runs along the top, Highland Avenue and Linden cross the left half diagonally, and Woodland Avenue and 3rd Avenue run north and south through the middle; Orchard Lane leaves the left edge and Bedford Avenue meets Haddonfield Avenue at the lower right. The land is divided into large numbered lots, mostly vacant, with scattered frame dwellings, a few stores at Chapel and Woodland Avenues, and many chicken coops and small sheds; one group of buildings stands near 3rd Avenue with a water tower. Along Haddonfield Avenue the lots east of the road are cut into narrow building lots. A heavy line in the lower middle of the page encloses a separate inset of an area in Pensauken Township (part 2).
notes: Haddonfield Avenue is Haddonfield Road (CR 644) today; Chapel Avenue is Chapel Avenue West, and Linden is Linden Street.
Bedford Avenue / Haddonfield Road is a hand-picked point.

100 ft. Two parts: 1 main map (Delaware Twp: Chapel Av, Harvard Av, Woodland Av, 3rd Av, Highland Av, Haddonfield Av = Haddonfield Rd); 2 inset in a heavy pentagon (Githens Av, N. Union Av, Cedar (Myrtle) Av, Union Av Lane, Pennsauken Twp), anchored on one hand-picked point.

sheet-35-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 35 is an inset enclosed by a heavy line in the lower middle of the page. It shows an area of Pensauken Township north of the rest of the sheet, drawn at 100 ft to an inch with its own north arrow pointing up and to the right. North Union Avenue runs up the left side of the inset, with Githens Avenue and Cedar (Myrtle) Avenue leaving it to the west and Union Avenue Lane and Short Lane running east into a large tract. The tract holds a few frame dwellings, one marked old and dilapidated, a poultry house, garages, sheds and coops; along Union Avenue Lane stand a few more dwellings, and the southern edge is the top of the area drawn on sheet 22.
notes: North Union Avenue is Union Avenue today.

Placed from one hand-picked point, Githens Avenue / Union Avenue, with the atlas scale (3.92 px/ft) and north 30 degrees right of up taken from the bearings of Githens and Union Avenues (the inset's arrow shows about 25): low confidence.
The modern Cedar Avenue / Union Avenue junction lies about 36 m south of Githens Avenue, closer to the drawn Union Avenue Lane than to Cedar (Myrtle) Avenue, so it was not used.

sheet-36.description: Sheet 36 covers the area south of the Merchantville borough in Pennsauken Township, drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned about 4 degrees so that north points up and slightly to the left. South Lexington Avenue runs from the top of the sheet down the middle, and then turns south-west toward the bottom of the sheet. Magnolia Avenue crosses the top edge and Wistaria Avenue crosses the upper third; the Roosevelt Public School, a large brown-coloured fire-proof building with its corridor and heating plant marked, stands on the block east of South Lexington Avenue just below Wistaria Avenue. To the left a diagonal road, Laurel Avenue, runs from the upper left corner, and to the right Florida Boulevard runs up the right side from the lower centre to the upper right with Magnolia, Wistaria, Laurel and Elvena Avenues crossing it at an angle. Between them the blocks are mostly small, with scattered dwellings along South Lexington Avenue and Elvena Avenue, and many numbered blocks left empty. The lower left is a regular grid of long blocks between Mansion Boulevard, Baker, Garfield, Bloomfield, Schleicher and Homestead Avenues with a few dwellings, and the Bloomfield Park Volunteer Fire Co. No. 1 stands at Baker Avenue near the right edge. The left and bottom margins are marked no exposure. A compass rose stands at the left, and the scale bar at the bottom right. A note at the upper left gives the angle of a bend in the street.
notes: Wistaria Avenue is Wisteria Avenue today; South Lexington Avenue is Lexington Avenue; South Springfield Avenue is Springfield Avenue.
Magnolia Avenue is lettered both at the top of the sheet and on the diagonal street at the upper right.
The Laurel Avenue and Magnolia Avenue junction at the upper left lies about 12 m from its drawn position and was not used.
Part of the street at the upper right is marked not open.
100 ft. Turned +4 deg. Bloomfield area: S. Lexington, Florida Blvd, Mansion Blvd (ink 30 on the part).

sheet-37.description: Sheet 37 is drawn at 100 ft to an inch and turned so that north points up and to the left, as the compass at the top shows. It lies in the south-western part of Pensauken Township, south of the area of sheet 26. South Browning Road runs down the page a little left of centre. West of it, between Garfield (Villa) Avenue and Schleicher Avenue, a block numbered 457 is divided into narrow lots, and below Schleicher Avenue the Pensauken Township Sewage Disposal Plant occupies blocks 459 and 461 with its settling basins, septic tanks and pump house. Further down, Burrwood Avenue is lined with two rows of small detached dwellings, and Witherspoon, Garden and Royal Avenues are drawn as wide streets between large empty blocks numbered 680 to 683. East of South Browning Road, Homestead Avenue runs off to the right across the upper part of the sheet with a few dwellings along it, crossed by Sinkinson Avenue and Plymouth Road. At the centre of the right half stands the Camden County Vocational School, a large group of brick buildings with shops, gymnasium and swimming pool, boiler room and hose connections, with a greenhouse and buried fuel tanks beside it. Below, Witherspoon, Garden and Caroline Avenues cross a mostly blank area of blocks numbered 684 to 688 with a few dwellings along South Browning Road and Caroline Avenue. Neighbouring sheets are keyed 25 and 26.
notes: Burrwood Avenue is Burwood Avenue in OpenStreetMap; South Browning Road is Browning Road.
Placed from five points only, four of them on South Browning Road (Garfield, Homestead, Burwood and Royal Avenues) and one hand-picked on Homestead Avenue at Sinkinson Avenue: low confidence.

Witherspoon Avenue, Garden Avenue and Plymouth Avenue were left out of the fit: the drawn blocks are evenly spaced (about 300 ft) while the modern junctions on Browning Road are not, and the modern Plymouth Avenue lies about 15 m east of the drawn Plymouth Road.
100 ft. Turned -32 deg. Browning Rd, Camden County Vocational School, sewage plant; 4 of 5 points on Browning Rd (low confidence).
